Solve the following optimization problem using Gurobi. 

Subject: Portfolio allocation brief — maximizing strategic impact under operational and compliance limits

Team,

For the upcoming planning cycle, we need to size six scalable initiatives to maximize our overall Strategic Impact score while staying within our operational capacities and compliance balances. Each initiative can be deployed fractionally (we are not restricted to whole units) within the specific range noted below, and each has a defined per‑unit contribution to value and to our capacity/compliance balances. Some balances are measured relative to a baseline and are framed as “net” positions; where those limits are negative, they represent required net reductions.

Initiative 1 — Rooftop Solar Rollout
- Scale: We may commission anywhere from 0 up to 8.61 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 9.86 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: No draw.
- Net carbon balance: Lowers the balance by 4.6 tCO2e per unit (helps us meet the required net reduction).
- Nitrate discharge balance: No change.
- Skilled technician hours: Requires 3.1 thousand hours per unit.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No draw.
- Net landfill mass: Lowers the balance by 2.71 tons per unit (additional diversion relative to baseline).
- Community noise index: Reduces the index by 0.24 points per unit.

Initiative 2 — Waste‑to‑Energy Operations Expansion
- Scale: We may deploy anywhere from 0 up to 6.1 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 1.8 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: No draw.
- Net carbon balance: No change.
- Nitrate discharge balance: No change.
- Skilled technician hours: No draw.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No draw.
- Net landfill mass: Lowers the balance by 6.28 tons per unit (significant diversion benefit).
- Community noise index: Increases the index by 5.88 points per unit (community impact to manage).

Initiative 3 — Smart Controls and Distributed Storage
- Scale: We may deploy anywhere from 0 up to 17.75 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 9.36 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: No draw.
- Net carbon balance: No change.
- Nitrate discharge balance: No change.
- Skilled technician hours: Frees up 1.95 thousand hours per unit (reduces demand on our skilled workforce).
- Grid interconnection capacity: Uses 7.3 capacity units per deployment unit.
- Net landfill mass: No change.
- Community noise index: Reduces the index by 0.17 points per unit.

Initiative 4 — High‑Efficiency Boiler Retrofits
- Scale: We may deploy anywhere from 0 up to 14.43 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 5.63 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: No draw.
- Net carbon balance: Lowers the balance by 4.9 tCO2e per unit.
- Nitrate discharge balance: No change.
- Skilled technician hours: Requires 1.67 thousand hours per unit.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No draw.
- Net landfill mass: No change.
- Community noise index: No change.

Initiative 5 — Water Reclamation Plant Upgrade
- Scale: We may deploy anywhere from 0 up to 16.86 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 5.43 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: Draws 3.71 million of the capital budget per unit.
- Net carbon balance: Lowers the balance by 5.06 tCO2e per unit.
- Nitrate discharge balance: Lowers the balance by 8.75 kg N per unit.
- Skilled technician hours: No draw.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No draw.
- Net landfill mass: No change.
- Community noise index: Reduces the index by 1.97 points per unit.

Initiative 6 — Recycling Logistics Enhancement
- Scale: We may deploy anywhere from 0 up to 19.47 units.
- Strategic value: Each unit contributes 8.25 points to the Strategic Impact score.
- Capital budget: No draw.
- Net carbon balance: No change.
- Nitrate discharge balance: No change.
- Skilled technician hours: No draw.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No draw.
- Net landfill mass: Lowers the balance by 1.27 tons per unit.
- Community noise index: No change.

Compliance and capacity limits (must not be exceeded)
- Capital budget availability: At most 37.68 million is available for capital outlays.
- Net carbon balance (relative to baseline): Must be at or below −124.45 tCO2e (i.e., at least 124.45 tons of net abatement).
- Nitrate discharge balance (relative to baseline): Must be at or below −83.73 kg N (i.e., at least 83.73 kg of net reduction).
- Skilled technician hours: No more than 21.64 thousand hours are available.
- Grid interconnection capacity: No more than 72.83 capacity units are available.
- Net landfill mass (relative to baseline): Must be at or below −61.46 tons (i.e., at least 61.46 tons of net diversion).
- Community noise index: Must not exceed 8.02 index points.

Our objective is to configure the above six initiatives within their respective ranges so that the total Strategic Impact score is as high as possible while honoring every limit listed. Please use this brief to guide scenario development and come back with the recommended mix.

    m.addConstr(7.3 * vars['Var_2'] <= 72.83, name='C4')
    m.addConstr(-2.71 * vars['Var_0'] + -6.28 * vars['Var_1'] + -1.27 * vars['Var_5'] <= -61.46, name='C5')
    m.addConstr(-0.24 * vars['Var_0'] + 5.88 * vars['Var_1'] + -0.17 * vars['Var_2'] + -1.97 * vars['Var_4'] <= 8.02, name='C6')

Solve the following optimization problem using Gurobi. 

Subject: Proposed mix to minimize relief spend while meeting service commitments

Team,

We need to set the spring deployment mix across six supply lines so we meet our grant-mandated minimum service levels at the lowest possible total spend. With the exception of one bulk line item that can be split, all orders must be placed in whole lots. Below is the working brief on each lever and how it contributes to our five service commitments: Sustenance, Hygiene, Water, Shelter, and Medical readiness.

- Ordering rules: anywhere from 0 up to 14.56 lots, placed only in whole-lot increments.
- Cost profile: 2.97 per lot on our internal cost index.
- Service impact per lot:
  • Sustenance: +8.25 credits
  • Hygiene: +5.17 coverage points
  • Water: +1.59 supply units
  • Shelter: +1.11 capacity units
  • Medical: no credit
- Notes: This is our most balanced nutrition-forward option with light spillover into hygiene, water, and shelter but does not move the needle on medical readiness.

2) Hydration & First-Aid Cases
- Ordering rules: anywhere from 0 up to 16.4 lots, placed only in whole-lot increments.
- Cost profile: 6.27 per lot.
- Service impact per lot:
  • Sustenance: +1.42 credits
  • Hygiene: no coverage credit
  • Water: +3.15 supply units
  • Shelter: no capacity credit

- Notes: Strong for water and medical; limited effect on sustenance; does not help hygiene or shelter.

3) Shelter–Water Modules

- Cost profile: 2.40 per lot.
- Service impact per lot:
  • Sustenance: no credit
  • Hygiene: +2.88 coverage points
  • Water: +9.01 supply units
  • Shelter: +8.45 capacity units

4) Balanced Relief Bundles

6) Community Hygiene Kits

  • Sustenance: +1.49 credits

  • Shelter: no capacity credit

- Hygiene: at least 102.82 coverage points in total
- Water: at least 120.26 supply units in total
- Shelter: at least 56.74 capacity units in total
- Medical readiness: at least 104.58 points in total

    m.addConstr(6.45 * vars['Var_1'] + 6.31 * vars['Var_2'] + -2.42 * vars['Var_3'] + 6.53 * vars['Var_4'] + -1.08 * vars['Var_5'] <= 51.23, name='C4')

  Each FTE contributes 5.01 units toward Training & Certification Hours, 0.53 toward Quality Assurance Audits, 1.52 toward Emergency Response Coverage, and 4.32 toward Rural Outreach Mileage. These FTEs do not move On‑Call Baseline Coverage, Client Appointments Completed, or Specialist Case Closures.

- Digital Academy Seats (no minimum commitment; up to 16.76 seat‑equivalents; $4.94 per seat‑equivalent)
  Each seat delivers 8.36 units toward Training & Certification Hours only. There is no effect on On‑Call Baseline Coverage, Client Appointments Completed, Quality Assurance Audits, Specialist Case Closures, Emergency Response Coverage, or Rural Outreach Mileage.

- Core Field Crew Hires (no minimum commitment; up to 14.43 crews; whole crews only; $5.77 per crew)

- Agency Surge Blocks (no minimum commitment; up to 10.32 blocks; $1.85 per block)
  Each block adds 0.23 units to On‑Call Baseline Coverage, 8.62 to Client Appointments Completed, and 6.29 to Emergency Response Coverage. There is no impact on Training & Certification Hours, Quality Assurance Audits, Specialist Case Closures, or Rural Outreach Mileage.

- Specialist Strike Team Months (no minimum commitment; up to 8.25 team‑months; $7.08 per team‑month)
  Each team‑month contributes 9.22 Client Appointments Completed, 9.99 Training & Certification Hours, 8.68 Quality Assurance Audits, 1.17 Emergency Response Coverage, and 9.36 Rural Outreach Mileage. These teams do not affect On‑Call Baseline Coverage or Specialist Case Closures.

- Rural Outreach Van‑Days (no minimum commitment; up to 14.32 vehicle‑days; $7.02 per vehicle‑day)
  Each vehicle‑day delivers 3.26 units of On‑Call Baseline Coverage, 9.26 Quality Assurance Audits, and 9.81 Rural Outreach Mileage. There is no contribution to Client Appointments Completed, Training & Certification Hours, Specialist Case Closures, or Emergency Response Coverage.

Our optimization will minimize total spend across the six levers above while honoring these floors. Note that Blue‑Shift Flex FTEs, Digital Academy Seats, Agency Surge Blocks, Specialist Strike Team Months, and Rural Outreach Van‑Days can be dialed in fractionally within their ranges, whereas Core Field Crew Hires must be contracted as whole crews and cannot exceed 14.43 crews.
